dependencies.quote: The firm-specific weekly return, denoted by W, is defined as the natural log of one plus the residual return from the following expanded market model regression

CRASHt+1 is an indicator variable equal to one if a firm experiences one or more firm-specific weekly returns falling 3.2 or more standard deviations below the mean firm-specific weekly return for fiscal year t + 1, and zero otherwise
NCSKEWt is the negative coefficient of skewness of firm-specific weekly returns in fiscal year t
SIGMAt is the standard deviation of firm-specific weekly returns in fiscal year t
RETt is the average firm-specific weekly return in fiscal year t times 100
COORDINATOR-VERIFIED MATHEMATICAL TRANSCRIPTION (Firm-specific weekly return conversion, physical PDF page 15): W_j,tau = ln(1 + epsilon_j,tau).

scope.quote: We measure conditional conservatism using Basu’s (1997) asymmetric timeliness coefficient, Ball and Shivakumar’s (2005) accrual-based measure of asymmetric timeliness, and Khan and Watts’ (2009) firm–year measure of conditional conservatism.
To test whether more conservative firms experience lower crash risk, we first estimate the following augmented Basu (1997) model following the method of Francis and Martin (2010):
Model (2) reports the results of estimating Eq. (9) with firm fixed effects
and all other control variables except OPAQUE

The display labels the focal triple interaction beta_7; the surrounding prose instead refers to beta_8.
We also replace CRASH with NCSKEW in Eq. (9) to examine the relation between conservatism and negative firm-specific return skewness.

dependencies.quote: The firm-specific weekly return, denoted by W, is defined as the natural log of one plus the residual return from the following expanded market model regression

CRASHt+1 is an indicator variable equal to one if a firm experiences one or more firm-specific weekly returns falling 3.2 or more standard deviations below the mean firm-specific weekly return for fiscal year t + 1, and zero otherwise
NCSKEWt is the negative coefficient of skewness of firm-specific weekly returns in fiscal year t
SIGMAt is the standard deviation of firm-specific weekly returns in fiscal year t
RETt is the average firm-specific weekly return in fiscal year t times 100
COORDINATOR-VERIFIED MATHEMATICAL TRANSCRIPTION (Firm-specific weekly return conversion, physical PDF page 15): W_j,tau = ln(1 + epsilon_j,tau).

Principal question selected from the abstract/introduction and Section 3 before reviewing the prior result: whether conditional conservatism predicts lower future crash risk. The paper tests this with Basu, Ball–Shivakumar, and Khan–Watts conservatism measures and both CRASH and NCSKEW proxies. Retained the full-sample full-control firm-fixed-effect columns (2) in Tables 3 and 4 and full-control column (2) in Table 5, with one model per primary proxy. Excluded reduced-sample OPAQUE columns, the Table 3/4 no-firm-fixed-effect comparisons, Table 5 controls-only columns, marginal-effect analysis, later information-asymmetry interactions, and robustness/time-trend tests.

The first-sweep result omitted the fitted expanded weekly market model (Equation (7)), although its residuals are transformed into W and generate the retained CRASH, NCSKEW, SIGMA, and RET variables. Added one repeated firm-year supporting fit and linked each dependent baseline to the W-derived variables it uses.
